title: Limits on control of commercial television and radio licences
summary: A person may control no more than one commercial television licence, and no more than two commercial radio licences, in the same licence area.
direction_rationale: Ownership limits within a licence area cap how many licences one owner may hold.

review.notes: Drafted by AI-assisted desk research on 17 November 2026 (phase 6 of the levers re-evaluation, batch 1) from the law quoted. Not yet checked: verify the description, industries and assessment before use.

assessment.summary: No one may control more than one commercial television licence, or more than two commercial radio licences, in the same licence area. The limits aim at diversity of voices; they also block mergers that might lower costs, and the number of licences in each area is itself limited.

marks.reason: Stops one owner taking every commercial licence in an area.
Blocks consolidation within a licence area, which could lower costs for regional broadcasters.

assessment.confidence_note: Whether the limits raise or lower productivity is contested; the marks offset.

responsible.note: Not checked against the administrative arrangements order.
The ACMA applies the control rules.
